Why do you think men are significantly more prone to suicide than women?

The suicide gender gap has to do with preferred methods. The methods chosen by men tend to be more lethal. If all suicide methods had a 100% success rate, more women would die. The question is, do men choose more lethal methods because they have a greater desire to die, and (conversely) do women choose less lethal methods as a 'cry for help'? There are probably cultural and biological factors at play (are women less likely to want to inflict disfiguring injuries on themselves? are men more likely to see themselves as a 'burden' on society, given their lower baseline reproductive value? etc.)
